lines: Dusk. The lamps going up. The fog coming in off the Mere.
She puts the kettle on when the lamps go up. I am punctual. She is predictable. The arrangement works.
Tonight calls for a gift. A vole, ideally. Voles say what flowers cannot.
There. Under the chimney pot. Fat, smug, unaware.
A hunt begins before the first claw: in the going-in.
Quietly, then. Or loudly. But *deliberately*.

hints.1: Choose your APPROACH: spend Shadow to Stalk (it wastes its first move; your first hit cuts deeper) — or spend other energy another way. Then: Pounce costs 2 Ferocity. Scratch is free, once per turn.
hints.2: Energy spent is gone for the whole prowl. Watch the spool.

lines: Acquired. Thoughtfully dead. She will say 'not on the table', and mean 'thank you'.
Eight bells from the tower. There is no ninth bell. Someone should look into that.
Between the chimneys: a thread of silver light, thin as a hair, humming. Not mine. Not hers.
I did not chase it. I am a professional.
Something small and hungry drifts up from the gutter, eyeing the vole.
The vole is not up for discussion.

hints.1: The wisp telegraphs its next move up top — the little hand icon means it steals CARDS. Spend what you can't protect.
hints.2: End your turn in the sun when you can: a sunbeam returns a spent card to your deck.
hints.3: Its 'Covet' wants what you're holding. A banked card is a promise — and a target.

lines: Street level. Too quiet. No pigeons. Pigeons are never quiet; that is their entire profession.
The lamps on Needle Lane are lit wrong. The Lamplighters never miss.
The shadows here are deep enough to wear. So I will wear them.

hints.1: New skill: SLINK — Shadow energy, Block 3. The fog makes Shadow cheaper on this street.
hints.2: Its Lunge hits for 4. Block BEFORE it lands. Or bank a card now and go big next turn — your risk to price.
hints.3: You could also have Stalked or Ambushed on the way in. Next fight, maybe.

lines: The dog and I have agreed to disagree.
The sting wants licking. The nerves want loafing. Dignity is negotiable at this hour.
And the quiet is still wrong. It is the quiet of a held breath.

hints.1: New: PURR heals 2 a turn for two turns — broken if you take damage. LOAF blocks 6 and commits all paws.
hints.2: This one is above your weight. SLIP AWAY costs nothing but pride — and a finished purr keeps you Warm into the next fight.
hints.3: You do not have to win this. You have to get home.

lines: Empty clothes, out walking. The owner missing. Not dead — missing.
And ahead, over the rooftops: her window. Dark.
Her window is never dark.
Two ways home from here.
The long way passes the Lamplighters' silent hall — whatever went wrong tonight, it went wrong there first.
The fast way is over the fences. Now. While the kettle still screams.
choices: The long way — see what silenced the lamps

lines: The Lamplighters' hall: door open, ladders racked, kettle cold. Nobody. Nothing. Except—
Caught on a lamp-hook: a thread of silver. HER stitching. She was here tonight. Why was she HERE?
I take the thread. It hums against my teeth like a struck bell.
(Her Stitching joins your deck — Moonlight 2.)
Over the fences, under the gate, up the drainpipe I have used nine hundred times.
Fast. Faster than anything on four legs tonight.
Fast enough that something inside is still... busy.
The door: shut. A door has never once been an obstacle. It is, however, always an insult.
In through the workroom window.
The threads on the walls — cut. All of them. Hanging like torn hems.
Something is standing in the parlor doorway, wearing the room.
The parlor. The kettle, screaming on the stove.
Elspeth in her chair. The light gone out of her hands.
I took the kettle off the fire. One paw. It took three tries.
Nobody will ever know.
The thread at my chest — the one that was always hers — cut.
Not quite.
One strand left. Thin as spite. Running out under the window, into the city.
Then that is where we are going.

hollow_court_first: A desk. A lamp. A queue of one.
'Name?' — I am a cat. — '...Vane's familiar. Nine allotted, one spent.'
'First visit is complimentary. Do try to make the others interesting.'
The stamp comes down. It is, I notice, a paw print. Neither of us remarks on this.
hollow_court_repeat: The desk again. The lamp again. The Clerk does not look up.
'Back so soon. The form remembers you, which saves us both time.'
The Toll is taken. Professionally. Almost gently.
The stairs up are longer than the fall down. They always are.
unpicked_won: It comes apart. Thread by thread. That was not supposed to happen.
Somewhere below the city, a clerk files something under 'irregular'.
